messages:
erin: We need a clear pattern for private connectivity when control plane is central + regional dataplane. Choices: PrivateLink default, or paid preserve-ip addon (ENI agent). Quick pros/cons?

ash: PrivateLink scales and is self-serve but NATs egress (loses src ip). ENI-agent preserves src ip but needs cross-account ENI attach and more ops.

mike: Also note peering is route-preserving but hits route table limits at scale. Not ideal for many small tenants.

zoe: For preserve-ip addon we should require a scheduled maintenance window and limited IAM template. Can't force ENI attach without customer approval.

erin: Agreed. Product proposal: default = PrivateLink; optional preserve-ip = paid onboarding with agent + ENI. Documented tradeoffs for sales.

ash: Operational checklist for addon: IAM CFN, agent install script, verify ip-preserve test (curl with X-Orig-IP echo), monitoring exports to our tenant dashboard.

mike: Failure modes to call out: ENI detach race, route misconfig, and NLB AZ imbalance for PrivateLink. Include rollback steps: withdraw endpoint, revert route table, and DNS TTL short.

zoe: Small security note: agent must run least-privilege and have explicit uninstall hook to detach ENI cleanly.

infra-bot: Reminder: PI-345 spike has ENI attach median 90s across regions. Link: go/PI-345 (internal).

erin: Action items: erin draft onboarding matrix; ash build IAM template; mike write failure-mode runbook; zoe add security checklist. We'll merge into one cutover-playbook.
